subject: general
question: In August 2025, the first phase of the Darwin Tree of Life (DToL) project neared completion. What is the primary aim of this international biodiversity initiative?

options.text: To sequence the genomes of all eukaryotic species in Britain and Ireland
To decode the genetic basis of rare diseases in isolated human populations
To engineer climate-resilient crops using data from ancestral plant genomes
To map human migration patterns through ancient DNA found in fossils

solution:
The correct answer is __**To sequence the genomes of all eukaryotic species in Britain and Ireland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Darwin Tree of Life (DToL) project** is a pioneering scientific initiative aimed at **sequencing the genomes of all 70,000 eukaryotic species** found in **Britain and Ireland**.
 
• Launched in **October 2019**, the project reached a major milestone in **August 2025** as it neared the completion of its **first phase**, which involved establishing high-quality reference genomes for key families of organisms.
 
• The primary objective of the **DToL** is to provide a complete genetic catalog of biodiversity, which helps scientists understand **evolutionary relationships**, **ecosystem dynamics**, and the **genetic health** of species. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• Unlike human-centric genomic studies, this project focuses on **eukaryotes**, which encompass all complex life forms including **animals, plants, fungi, and protists**, while excluding bacteria and archaea.
